props applied this boot
Presets
AVB / vbmeta
Android Verified Boot metadata props. {vbmeta_size} expands to the randomised size stored in config.sh; {avb_version} expands to the avb_version key, so the two AVB version props can never drift apart.
7 rules · 10-vbmeta.prop
Edit rules
Verified boot state
Reports the bootloader as locked with verity enforcing, and clears the MediaTek orange-state marker.
5 rules · 20-verified-boot.prop
Edit rules
Verified boot errors
Removes the AVB error/diagnostic props some devices leave behind. These are deleted rather than blanked - for a prop like this, existing at all is the signal.
4 rules · 25-verified-boot-errors.prop
Edit rules
Warranty bit
Clears the warranty/KNOX-style tripped flags.
4 rules · 30-warranty.prop
Edit rules
Debuggable / secure
Presents the build as a non-debuggable, secure production build.
4 rules · 40-debuggable.prop · runs at post-fs-data
Edit rules
Mock location
Reports mock locations as disallowed. Its own preset because anyone deliberately using a location-spoofing app wants this off while keeping the other presets on.
1 rule · 44-mock-location.prop
Edit rules
Build type
Reports a user build signed with release-keys instead of userdebug/test-keys.
3 rules · 50-build-type.prop · runs at post-fs-data
Edit rules
Security patch level
Report a current security patch date, so a stale one on a custom ROM isn't a flag. OS -> current YYYY-MM-01, vendor -> YYYY-MM-05 (stepped back a month on the 1st-4th so it's never a future date). Off by default: a patch date newer than this build's fingerprint is itself an inconsistency, so enable knowingly. 'reset' only rewrites a prop that already exists and differs.
2 rules · 52-security-patch.prop · runs at post-fs-data
Edit rules
Build date consistency
Copy this device's own ro.build.date / ro.build.date.utc to every per-partition variant, so they can't disagree (a cross-partition mismatch is itself a signal). 'same_as' reads the source prop's live value and only writes a target that already exists, so a partition the device lacks is never invented. Off by default.
19 rules · 53-build-date.prop
Edit rules
Verified boot hash (advanced)
Pin ro.boot.vbmeta.digest to a specific value. Fill a real known-good digest into the rule line below, remove its leading '# ', and set 'enabled: 1'. A wrong or blank value is worse than the device's own, so this ships disabled with the rule commented - enabling alone does nothing until you edit it.
0 rules · 54-verified-boot-hash.prop
Edit rules
OEM unlock (SDK <= 35)
Hides that OEM unlocking is permitted, by zeroing the prop. Android 16 changed how this prop is read - see 61-oem-unlock-sdk36.prop, which handles SDK 36 and up instead.
1 rule · 60-oem-unlock.prop · SDK 35 and below
Edit rules
OEM unlock (SDK 36+)
On Android 16 and up, sys.oem_unlock_allowed is deleted rather than set to 0, because from that release the prop's presence is what gets read.
1 rule · 61-oem-unlock-sdk36.prop · SDK 36+
Edit rules
Custom & <odd> name
A user preset with every header
2 rules · 65-custom.prop · runs at post-fs-data · SDK 30-35
Edit rules
No enabled header
1 rule · 66-no-enabled.prop · runs at boot-completed · SDK 34+
Edit rules
67-bare
1 rule · 67-bare.prop
Edit rules
Vendor-specific (Xiaomi / Realme)
Lock-state props used by MIUI/HyperOS and Realme UI. Harmless on other brands - 'reset' never creates a prop the device doesn't already have, so this is a no-op on e.g. Samsung.
3 rules · 70-oem-vendor.prop
Edit rules
Recovery bootmode
Masks having booted from recovery. Uses 'contains', so only values that actually mention recovery are rewritten.
3 rules · 80-recovery-bootmode.prop
Edit rules
ADB state
Masks a live adbd. Runs at boot-completed, once Android has finished booting and init has written these props. Turn it off if you rely on tooling that reads adb state props.
4 rules · 85-adb-state.prop · runs at boot-completed
Edit rules
USB config
Reports the USB mode as MTP rather than ADB. Kept separate from the ADB state preset so either can be turned off alone.
1 rule · 86-usb-config.prop
Edit rules
Emulator / cloud phone
Blanks the qemu marker some detection libraries read to spot emulators.
1 rule · 90-emulator.prop
Edit rules
Encryption state
Reports userdata as encrypted.
1 rule · 95-encryption.prop
Edit rules
Crash recovery counter
Removes the Android 15+ crashrecovery rescue-boot counter, which is non-zero only after a boot loop. A no-op on devices that don't have it.
1 rule · 96-crashrecovery.prop
Edit rules
Build fingerprint
Rewrites userdebug to user in ro.build.fingerprint and strips custom-ROM names from it. OFF by default - read the warning below before enabling.
4 rules · 97-fingerprint.prop · runs at post-fs-data
Edit rules
Custom ROM props
Removes props that name the custom ROM you are running. OFF by default - the name pattern needs checking against your own device first.
2 rules · 98-rom-props.prop
Edit rules
New preset

page_settings:
Language
Interface language
English is the source language. Other languages are community translations and may be incomplete; missing text falls back to English.
English
Property spoofing
Prop backend
The stock resetprop is the default. resetprop-rs applies changes as stealth writes and count-preserving deletes (--nuke), leaving no serial or gap trace — switch to Auto (uses it when the bundled/downloaded binary works, else stock) or resetprop-rs to opt in. When resetprop-rs is active the rebuild option below is not needed and is skipped.
Stock resetprop (default)
Auto (resetprop-rs if available)
resetprop-rs (stealth)
Rebuild prop areas after changes
Only used with the stock resetprop. Deleting a prop leaves a reclaimable hole in property storage; this compacts it. "Touched areas only" rebuilds just the areas Nyx changed; "All areas" can log harmless errors on devices with an unparseable area (e.g. telephony props). Reclaims the storage gap, not serial counters. Ignored when resetprop-rs is the backend.
Touched areas only (recommended)
All areas
Off
Prop-preset repeat loop
Master switch for the background loop that periodically re-applies any preset carrying a '# repeat:' header, for the rare prop that resets after boot. Turning it off stops the loop without a reboot. Inactive unless a preset opts in, and the loop is itself a detection signal, so leave it on only when a preset actually needs it.
Updates
Skip resetprop-rs update check on open
On by default. Turn it off and opening the WebUI compares the installed resetprop-rs binary against the latest release, then offers to install it — nothing is ever replaced without asking.
Check resetprop-rs now
Compares hashes against the latest Enginex0/resetprop-rs release for this device's ABI. Works whether or not the check on open is enabled.
Check
Presets live in the Props section. Most changes take effect on the next reboot.

Credits
NyxProps is the prop-spoofing companion to NyxSUSFS. The two are separate modules, so each can be installed and updated on its own. It does not need SuSFS.
The default backend is resetprop from Magisk by topjohnwu, as shipped with KernelSU.
NyxProps bundles resetprop-rs by Enginex0 (MIT) as an optional stealth prop backend. Thank you for a great tool.
A number of the prop-spoofing ideas were sparked by studying BRENE by rrr333nnn333. The ideas were reimplemented in Nyx's own way, but the inspiration deserves a shout-out.
The WebUI, the preset system and the glue I built myself, with love for the community. Issues and translations welcome.

new_file.template:
# name: My preset
# description: What this preset does
# enabled: 1
# Optional headers. Headers are read only from the block of # lines at
# the very top, so add them next to name/description/enabled, before
# the first blank line:
# stage: post-fs-data run BEFORE zygote. Needed for build-identity
# props the framework caches into android.os.Build
# (ro.build.type, ro.build.fingerprint,
# ro.build.version.security_patch, ro.debuggable),
# so the Java value matches the property.
# stage: boot-completed run from KernelSU's boot-completed stage. It
# starts when Android finishes booting, side by
# side with the default stage below.
# (no stage header) the service stage: waits until Android has
# finished booting, then applies, so the
# system's own boot-time writes can't undo it.
# min_sdk: 36 only run on this Android API level or above
# max_sdk: 35 only run on this Android API level or below
# To re-apply a preset periodically (for a prop something RESETS after
# boot) add a header line reading exactly: repeat: 120 (N seconds, no
# leading words). Off unless added. It starts one background process,
# which is itself detectable, so only use it for a prop you've confirmed
# reverts. Clamped to repeat_min_interval in config.sh.
# format: <mode> <prop> <value>
# missing set only if the prop is absent
# reset set only if present AND different (never creates)
# missing_match set if absent, or present and different
# contains <prop> <needle> <value> (replace the WHOLE value if
# it contains needle)
# clear <prop> (blank it if it has a value)
# delete <prop> (remove it entirely - not the
# same as clear)
# replace <prop> <needle> [value] (rewrite a substring of the
# current value; omit value to
# delete the substring)
# delete_matching <ere> (delete every prop whose NAME
# matches the pattern)
# same_as <prop> <source-prop> (set prop to another prop's
# live value; only if prop
# already exists; multi-word safe)
#
# Value tokens (resolved when the preset is applied):
# {avb_version} device AVB version {vbmeta_size} configured vbmeta size
# {security_patch} current YYYY-MM-01 {yyyy_mm} current YYYY-MM
# {vendor_patch} current YYYY-MM-05, rolled back a month until the 5th
# arrives, so it never names a future date
# reset ro.example.prop somevalue

refreshed_settings:
Language
Interface language
English is the source language. Other languages are community translations and may be incomplete; missing text falls back to English.
English
Property spoofing
Prop backend
The stock resetprop is the default. resetprop-rs applies changes as stealth writes and count-preserving deletes (--nuke), leaving no serial or gap trace — switch to Auto (uses it when the bundled/downloaded binary works, else stock) or resetprop-rs to opt in. When resetprop-rs is active the rebuild option below is not needed and is skipped.
Stock resetprop (default)
Auto (resetprop-rs if available)
resetprop-rs (stealth)
Rebuild prop areas after changes
Only used with the stock resetprop. Deleting a prop leaves a reclaimable hole in property storage; this compacts it. "Touched areas only" rebuilds just the areas Nyx changed; "All areas" can log harmless errors on devices with an unparseable area (e.g. telephony props). Reclaims the storage gap, not serial counters. Ignored when resetprop-rs is the backend.
Touched areas only (recommended)
All areas
Off
Prop-preset repeat loop
Master switch for the background loop that periodically re-applies any preset carrying a '# repeat:' header, for the rare prop that resets after boot. Turning it off stops the loop without a reboot. Inactive unless a preset opts in, and the loop is itself a detection signal, so leave it on only when a preset actually needs it.
Updates
Skip resetprop-rs update check on open
On by default. Turn it off and opening the WebUI compares the installed resetprop-rs binary against the latest release, then offers to install it — nothing is ever replaced without asking.
Check resetprop-rs now
Compares hashes against the latest Enginex0/resetprop-rs release for this device's ABI. Works whether or not the check on open is enabled.
Check
Presets live in the Props section. Most changes take effect on the next reboot.

Credits
NyxProps is the prop-spoofing companion to NyxSUSFS. The two are separate modules, so each can be installed and updated on its own. It does not need SuSFS.
The default backend is resetprop from Magisk by topjohnwu, as shipped with KernelSU.
NyxProps bundles resetprop-rs by Enginex0 (MIT) as an optional stealth prop backend. Thank you for a great tool.
A number of the prop-spoofing ideas were sparked by studying BRENE by rrr333nnn333. The ideas were reimplemented in Nyx's own way, but the inspiration deserves a shout-out.
The WebUI, the preset system and the glue I built myself, with love for the community. Issues and translations welcome.

Language
Interface language
English is the source language. Other languages are community translations and may be incomplete; missing text falls back to English.
English
Property spoofing
Prop backend
The stock resetprop is the default. resetprop-rs applies changes as stealth writes and count-preserving deletes (--nuke), leaving no serial or gap trace — switch to Auto (uses it when the bundled/downloaded binary works, else stock) or resetprop-rs to opt in. When resetprop-rs is active the rebuild option below is not needed and is skipped.
Stock resetprop (default)
Auto (resetprop-rs if available)
resetprop-rs (stealth)
Rebuild prop areas after changes
Only used with the stock resetprop. Deleting a prop leaves a reclaimable hole in property storage; this compacts it. "Touched areas only" rebuilds just the areas Nyx changed; "All areas" can log harmless errors on devices with an unparseable area (e.g. telephony props). Reclaims the storage gap, not serial counters. Ignored when resetprop-rs is the backend.
Touched areas only (recommended)
All areas
Off
Prop-preset repeat loop
Master switch for the background loop that periodically re-applies any preset carrying a '# repeat:' header, for the rare prop that resets after boot. Turning it off stops the loop without a reboot. Inactive unless a preset opts in, and the loop is itself a detection signal, so leave it on only when a preset actually needs it.
Updates
Skip resetprop-rs update check on open
On by default. Turn it off and opening the WebUI compares the installed resetprop-rs binary against the latest release, then offers to install it — nothing is ever replaced without asking.
Check resetprop-rs now
Compares hashes against the latest Enginex0/resetprop-rs release for this device's ABI. Works whether or not the check on open is enabled.
Check
Presets live in the Props section. Most changes take effect on the next reboot.
